breakfast.name: Trinxat (Potato and Cabbage Cake)
instructions: Boil potatoes and cabbage until tender
Drain and mash together roughly
Fry bacon until crisp, set aside
Sauté garlic in bacon fat, add potato-cabbage mix
Press into cake, cook until golden on both sides
Top with bacon
breakfast.description: Hearty Andorran mountain dish of mashed potatoes and cabbage fried until crispy.

breakfast.name: Coca de Recapte (Vegetable Flatbread)
instructions: Roll out bread dough into rectangle
Roast peppers and grill eggplant
Arrange vegetables over dough
Drizzle with olive oil, add thyme and salt
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes
breakfast.description: Catalan-influenced flatbread topped with roasted vegetables.

breakfast.name: Coques de Sucre (Sugar Flatbread)
instructions: Roll dough into flat oval shapes
Dimple with fingers, drizzle with oil
Sprinkle generously with sugar, anise, and pine nuts
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 min until edges are golden
breakfast.description: Sweet festival flatbread — baked for Sant Joan and village festes across the Pyrenees.

lunch.name: Escudella i Carn d'Olla
instructions: Boil meats in large pot 90 minutes
Add chickpeas, potatoes, carrots, turnip, cabbage
Cook 30 more minutes
Remove meats, slice on platter
Cook pasta in broth
Serve broth with pasta first, then meats and vegetables
lunch.description: Andorra's national dish — a rich two-course stew.

lunch.name: Truita de Carreroles (Wild Mushroom Omelette)
instructions: Slice mushrooms, sauté with garlic in olive oil
Beat eggs with salt and pepper
Pour over mushrooms
Cook until set, fold in half
Garnish with parsley
lunch.description: Simple Pyrenean omelette with prized wild mushrooms.

lunch.name: Embotits amb Mongetes (Sausage with White Beans)
instructions: Fry sausages whole until browned all over
In same pan, sauté garlic in oil
Add beans, warm through, season
Serve sausages on a bed of beans with parsley
lunch.description: Pyrenean comfort food — pork sausage with white beans, eaten on cold mountain evenings.

dinner.name: Cunillo (Braised Rabbit)
instructions: Brown rabbit in olive oil
Sauté onion and garlic
Add grated tomato, cook 10 min
Return rabbit, add wine and herbs
Braise covered on low 45 minutes
dinner.description: Traditional Andorran braised rabbit in tomato and wine.

dinner.name: Xai al Forn (Roast Lamb)
instructions: Season lamb with herbs
Place with potatoes and garlic in roasting pan
Add wine, drizzle oil
Roast at 180°C for 90 min, basting
Rest 10 min, serve with pan juices

dinner.name: Civet de Senglar (Wild Boar Stew)
instructions: Marinate boar in red wine with herbs and juniper overnight
Remove meat, pat dry, brown in oil
Sauté onion and carrot
Add flour, cook 2 min
Add marinade wine and bouquet garni
Return meat, bring to simmer
Cook low for 2-2.5 hours until meat falls apart
Stir in dark chocolate at the end — it deepens the sauce
Season and serve with mashed potatoes
dinner.description: Wild boar braised in red wine with dark chocolate — a Pyrenean hunter's stew made during autumn boar season.

dinner.name: Trinxat (Pyrenean Cabbage and Potato Cake)
ingredients: 200g salt pork belly or bacon (thick sliced)
instructions: Boil cabbage and potatoes together until very tender
Drain well and mash together — keep it rough, not smooth
Fry salt pork or bacon until crispy, set aside
In the pork fat, fry garlic briefly
Add the cabbage-potato mash to the pan
Press flat into a cake, fry until a crispy golden crust forms on the bottom
Flip (or finish under broiler) to crisp the other side
Top with the crispy pork
This is mountain survival food — Pyrenean shepherds' fuel for cold days
dinner.description: Andorra's mountain comfort food — mashed potato and cabbage fried into a crispy cake in pork fat, topped with crispy bacon. A Pyrenean shepherd's dish that went viral as 'the European bubble and squeak' — simple ingredients transformed by the crispy-crust technique.

snacks.name: Pa amb Tomàquet (Bread with Tomato)
instructions: Toast bread
Rub garlic over surface
Rub tomato pulp onto bread
Drizzle olive oil, add salt
snacks.description: The simplest and most beloved Pyrenean snack.

snacks.name: Embotits (Cured Meats Board)
instructions: Slice cured meats thinly
Rub bread with tomato and drizzle olive oil
Arrange meats, bread, and olives on board
snacks.description: An Andorran charcuterie board — small-production mountain-cured meats are a point of national pride.

desserts.name: Crema Andorrana
instructions: Heat milk with cinnamon and lemon zest
Whisk yolks with sugar and cornstarch
Temper with hot milk, return to heat
Stir until thickened, pour into ramekins
Chill, top with brown sugar and caramelize
desserts.description: Rich custard dessert similar to crema catalana.

desserts.name: Coca de Vidre (Glass Cake)
instructions: Mix flour with lard, eggs, sugar, anise, lemon zest
Roll very thin — it should be almost translucent (hence 'glass')
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 min until crispy
Dust with powdered sugar
Break into shards to serve
desserts.description: Paper-thin crispy cake so delicate it looks like stained glass — made for festivals.

drinks.name: Hot Chocolate
instructions: Chop chocolate
Heat milk with sugar
Dissolve cornstarch in cold milk, add
Add chocolate, stir until thick

drinks.name: Ratafia (Herbal Liqueur)
instructions: Quarter green walnuts, place in jar with herbs and spices
Pour spirit over, seal
Macerate 40 days, shaking weekly
Strain, dissolve sugar in warm water, add
Bottle and age 1 month

drinks.name: Vi Calent (Hot Wine)
instructions: Heat wine with spices and orange
Do not boil
Sweeten to taste
Serve in thick mugs
drinks.description: Andorra's version of mulled wine — drunk after skiing and during winter festivals.
